findings.location: library/pde/sobolev-poincare-and-morrey-inequalities-examples.md:28-32, second prose paragraph, radial-power discussion ending "so the p>n hypothesis cannot be extended to p=n"
findings.evidence: For fixed p>n the powers have exact Holder exponent alpha_0+delta, and their gradient energy diverges as delta tends to zero. This establishes the radial threshold for that fixed p, not failure of Morrey at p=n. At p=n, alpha_0=0 and the radial power is the constant 1 almost everywhere, which is a Sobolev class on the ball. The endpoint failure is established instead by the double-logarithm witness in cex-morrey-endpoint-p-equals-n-fails, already mentioned in the following clause. Attribute the endpoint conclusion to that witness and describe the powers as approaching the borderline. This is a short, locally resolvable prose inference repair, but B-page prose is read-only.
